name: Manufacture or delivery of a Penalty Group 1 controlled substance (under one gram)
officialTitle: OFFENSE: MANUFACTURE OR DELIVERY OF SUBSTANCE IN PENALTY GROUP 1.
conduct: Knowingly manufacturing, delivering, or possessing with intent to deliver a controlled substance listed in Penalty Group 1, in an aggregate amount of under one gram, including adulterants and dilutants. Chapter 481 authorizations apply. Delivery includes an actual or constructive transfer and an offer to sell. An offer-to-sell conviction requires corroboration by someone other than the offeree or by other evidence. Manufacture includes production, preparation, processing, packaging or labeling, subject to the practitioner exceptions in §481.002(25). Possession means actual care, custody, control or management. The substance, weight, alleged conduct and offense date must be established. The current drug schedules and punishment cannot automatically be applied to earlier conduct.
penalty: State jail felony: ordinarily 180 days to two years in a state jail and a possible fine up to $10,000. Qualifying deadly-weapon or prior-conviction findings can change punishment. A qualifying drug-free-zone finding under §481.134(b) or (d) increases punishment to a third-degree felony. Punishment increased under §481.134 must run consecutively to punishment for a conviction under another criminal statute. Under §481.140, using or attempting to use a person under 18 to commit or assist the offense raises punishment by one degree, or to first-degree felony punishment if force was used or threatened to gain the child’s assistance. Under §481.141, a finding that consumption of the substance manufactured or delivered caused death or serious bodily injury raises punishment by one degree. This increase is barred if the defendant is also prosecuted for §19.02(b)(4) murder in the same criminal episode. Either enhancement requires consecutive sentences. These conditions require their own findings.
